correctness.rationale: Circulant adjacency eigenvalues 2 cos(pi k/n)+t(−1)^k give the sharp unit-vector SDP bound by trace(A X)≥lambda_min tr(X). The alternating and two-dimensional extremal modes provide attaining Gram matrices. The latter eigenspace has only discrete sine/cosine modes, whose diagonal constraints force Q=I, proving uniqueness for t>1−cos(pi/n). A cut either crosses all 2n cycle edges (forcing zero antipodal cuts for even n) or misses at least two cycle edges; the explicit antiperiodic sign assignment attains 2n−2+nt. The rank-two vectors are all points of a regular 2n-gon, and any generic halfspace separates n consecutive points, crossing exactly 2n−2 cycle edges and all antipodal edges. Ratio monotonicity on each branch locates the unique maximizer; t=0, equality and t_sdp are handled. Independent brute-force CUT on 3≤n≤9 across five weights and Fourier-eigenvalue checks agreed (873760 masks/test instances).
residual_risks: Uniqueness and universal rounding exclude exactly the spectral crossing t=1−cos(pi/n) and degenerate normals; arbitrary nonuniform weights are not covered.

final_claim: For M_{2n} with unit cycle edges and weight t≥0 on n antipodal edges, odd n has CUT=SDP=n(2+t). For even n≥4, SDP changes at 1−cos(pi/n), integer CUT changes at 2/n, the ratio is maximized at 2/n, and above the SDP transition the unique rank-two optimal Gram matrix has deterministic generic hyperplane-rounding value 2n−2+nt (optimal integer iff t≥2/n).
